nodes.text: Suppose you want to connect your stereo to remote speakers. (a) If each wire must be 20 m long, what diameter copper wire should you use to keep the resistance less than 0.10 Ω per wire? (b) If the current to each speaker is 4.0 A, what is the potential difference, or voltage drop, across each wire?

nodes.figure_alternative: A stereo receiver connected to two remote speakers by separate copper-wire runs, each labeled 20 m.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: Part b. Voltage equals current times resistance, which equals 4.0 amperes times 0.10 ohm. The voltage drop V sub R is 0.400 volt, or 400 millivolts.

nodes.figure_alternative: Circuit sketch of a voltage source connected in series to the resistance of the wiring and a speaker. Arrows labeled I indicate clockwise conventional current.

nodes.normalized_math: \text{(a)}\quad \rho_{\mathrm{Cu}}=1.68\times10^{-8}\,\Omega\!\cdot\!\mathrm{m},\quad L=20\,\mathrm{m},\quad R=0.10\,\Omega;\qquad A=\pi r^2=\pi\left(\frac d2\right)^2;\qquad R=\rho\frac LA=\frac{4\rho L}{\pi d^2};\qquad d^2>\frac{4\rho L}{\pi R}\Rightarrow d>\left[\frac{4\rho L}{\pi R}\right]^{1/2}=\left[\frac{4(1.68\times10^{-8}\,\Omega\!\cdot\!\mathrm{m})(20\,\mathrm{m})}{\pi(0.10\,\Omega)}\right]^{1/2}=2.1\,\mathrm{mm}
nodes.spoken_math_alternative: Part a. The resistivity of copper is 1.68 times 10 to the negative 8 ohm meters, the length is 20 meters, and the resistance is 0.10 ohm. Area equals pi r squared, or pi times d over 2 squared. Resistance equals rho L over A, which equals 4 rho L over pi d squared. Therefore d squared must exceed 4 rho L over pi R, so d must exceed the square root of that quantity. Substitution gives 2.1 millimeters.
Power equals energy divided by time.
Electrical energy U equals charge q times voltage V.
Power equals charge times voltage divided by time, which equals current times voltage.
